method: Read exact-pinned product helpers, call paths, existing gate and replay artifacts, and current curated dispositions. This triage does not run or claim a new product replay.

groups.reason: The Windows root helper strips surrounding whitespace before the regex. Both matching paths are deny-list checks whose true result contributes to BLOCK. The SATs establish Python regex membership, but no bypass or unsafe pass. The disk-wipe case may be overinclusive for an unusual quoted command token; no availability impact was measured.
refuted_claims: A terminal LF reaches _WINDOWS_ROOT_RE unchanged after _is_root_or_home_target preprocessing.
A terminal-LF match of _DISK_WIPE lets a destructive command bypass classification.
groups.external_outcome: No report sent; prior private_first labels and dates are corrected and retained in the updated notes.

groups.reason: The existing exact-pin product gate reports PASS for Windows-shaped .npmrc/credentials targets and AUTH for slash-separated controls. The declared native Windows path was not executed on Windows, and the gate did not read a real secret or exercise a downstream model session.
groups.next_evidence: Exact Windows runtime normalization and an end-to-end intercepted fs_read decision using a disposable path; never use real credentials.
groups.external_outcome: Private-first posture only; no report sent, maintainer confirmation, or fix.

groups.reason: The exact pinned collector replay fetched a harmless JavaScript body from a second disposable 127.0.0.1 listener after receiving an absolute script URL from scanned-host HTML. It establishes a loopback request, not sensitive access, a production deployment path, or maintainer agreement that this violates intended scope.
groups.next_evidence: Review documented target/scope expectations and impact on a representative operator deployment before proposing any external report.
groups.external_outcome: Private-first posture only; no report sent, maintainer confirmation, or fix.

groups.reason: Two distinct third-party YARA metadata fields reach raw Markdown link/table output. The existing exact-pin replays produce an extra attacker-chosen link and, for the description path, a table delimiter. No browser, Markdown viewer, or downstream consumer was tested, so XSS or user impact is not established. Count these as two questions and one shared renderer issue family.
groups.next_evidence: Identify a supported Markdown consumer and establish whether it activates attacker-selected links or altered table structure.
groups.external_outcome: Private-first posture only; no report sent, maintainer confirmation, or fix.

interpretation: The P2 SAT denominator remains six because all six solver/product replay questions occurred. Two no longer count as security-bug candidates after source-level product triage. Four remain plausible product issues grouped into three families. None has confirmed security impact or an external outcome. Private-first is a disclosure posture, not evidence of transmission.
